(a) Maryland.—The table in section 2401(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (division B of Public Law 112–81; 125 Stat. 1672), is amended in the item relating to Fort Meade, Maryland, by striking “$29,640,000” in the amount column and inserting “$792,200,000”. 
    (b) Germany.—
        (1) Project authorization.—The table in section 2401(b) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (division B of Public Law 112–81; 125 Stat. 1673), is amended in the item relating to Rhine Ordnance Barracks, Germany, by striking “$750,000,000” in the amount column and inserting “$990,000,000”. 
        (2) Certification required.—The Secretary of Defense may not obligate additional funds made available pursuant to the amendment made by paragraph (1) until the Secretary certifies to the congressional defense committees that both of the following directly support the proposed scope for the hospital at the Rhine Ordnance Barracks, Germany:
            (A) A sufficient enduring beneficiary population. 
            (B) The fiscal year 2014 force structure assessment, incorporated in the budget submitted by the President to Congress for fiscal year 2014.

fable.w: The section amends military construction authorization amounts and bars obligating additional funds until the Secretary of Defense certifies certain facts to the congressional defense committees. The certification requirement can look like a procedural check on a federal decision, but Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted or given a right to object or sue.
fable.s: until the Secretary certifies to the congressional defense committees

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary of Defense to certify information to congressional defense committees before obligating funds. Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal to the government and does not involve outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.

opus.w: The only process in this section is a certification from the Secretary of Defense to the congressional defense committees, and both are inside the federal government. The other provisions just change authorized funding amounts for military construction projects. The certification condition looks procedural, but no one outside the federal government is consulted or involved, so it is not participation.
opus.s: The Secretary of Defense may not obligate additional funds made available pursuant to the amendment made by paragraph (1) until the Secretary certifies to the congressional defense committees
opus.b:
Step 1, the tempting reading: subsection (b)(2) is procedural. It stops the Secretary from spending the extra funds until he sends a certification, so it can look like a check on a federal decision. That reading fails because the certification goes to the congressional defense committees. Congress is inside the federal government. The rest of the section only changes dollar amounts for construction projects, and no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part in any decision.
